solutions.check: grid and clues read from the FT's printable PDF, its numbering matching the clue list; every fifteensquared answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Notice people in jumping event

parts.note: being given notice means getting the sack, dismissal from a job
a race is a people, an ethnic group

explanation.surface: An announcement about the competitors in a high-jump or long-jump contest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Notice' reads as an announcement but stands for the sack, as in being given one's notice at work.
explanation.definitionFit: A sports-day contest where competitors hop along inside sacks is a jumping event.

clue.text: Writer's attribute article ignored

indicators.note: something ignored is left out, so this letter is dropped from the verb

parts.note: to attribute something to someone is to ascribe it
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A quality belonging to an author, with an essay disregarded.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Writer's' is the definition plus 's (is). 'ignored' drops the article A from ASCRIBE.
explanation.definitionFit: A scribe was a copyist who wrote out documents by hand, so a writer.

clue.text: Express a very different opinion on huge canteens abroad

indicators.note: abroad here means scattered all over, so the letters are dispersed and rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone reverses their view about the enormous mess halls overseas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'abroad' rearranges ON HUGE CANTEENS, all fourteen letters, into the phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to alter one's stated views, typically completely, so to voice a contrary position.

clue.text: Continue to suppose parking's not available

indicators.note: something not available is absent, so its letter is taken away

parts.note: to suppose is to presume
P is the abbreviation for parking, as on road signs

explanation.surface: Keep going on the assumption that there is nowhere to park.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not available' removes P from PRESUME.
explanation.definitionFit: To resume is to carry on after a pause, a synonym of continue.

clue.text: Go over plot with grumpy type

parts.note: to go over a road or river is to cross it
a plot of land is a patch

explanation.surface: Walk across a garden allotment alongside an irritable person.
explanation.definitionFit: A crosspatch is an informal word for a bad-tempered, irritable person.

clue.text: Case enthralling court about music of the 1950s

indicators.note: about means turned round, so the whole combination is read backwards
enthralling means holding captive, so one word is held inside the other

parts.note: a pod is a case holding seeds
to court someone is to woo them

explanation.surface: A legal case captivates a court concerning a style of fifties pop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Case' suggests a lawsuit heard by a court, but it is a seed pod; the reversal of the combination is signalled by 'about'.
explanation.definitionFit: Doo-wop is a vocal harmony style of rhythm and blues popular in America in the 1950s.

clue.text: See 2
Circumspect about river worker giving guarantee

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the cautious word goes round the others

parts.note: circumspect means wary, cautious
R is the abbreviation for river on maps
an ant is the standard crossword worker, from the worker caste of the colony

explanation.surface: A cautious employee by the river gives an assurance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'worker' is the usual crossword ant; 'giving' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A warranty is a written promise from a maker to repair or replace faulty goods, a guarantee.

clue.text: Displaying name in short example

indicators.note: in places the abbreviation inside the shortened word
short means cut off at the end, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: a paradigm is a typical example or model

explanation.surface: Showing a signature in a brief illustration.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short' cuts the M from PARADIGM, and 'in' puts N inside PARADIG.
explanation.definitionFit: Parading something is showing it off, so displaying it.

clue.text: Word has spread about one's first promotional tour

indicators.note: spread about means scattered, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: first means the opening letter of the next word is taken

explanation.surface: News has circulated about someone's debut publicity trip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spread about' rearranges WORD HAS with O, the first letter of 'one's' taken by 'first'.
explanation.definitionFit: A roadshow is a touring event that travels from place to place to publicise something.

clue.text: Troublesome child treated, initially, by mistake

indicators.note: initially picks the opening letter of the word before it

parts.note: a mistake is an error

explanation.surface: A naughty child is dealt with first, in error.
explanation.walkthrough: 'initially' takes T from 'treated'; 'by' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A terror is an informal name for a mischievous, unruly youngster.

clue.text: Member of more than one union?

definitions.text: Member of more than one union?

parts.words: Member of more than one union?
parts.note: suggests someone belonging to several trade unions, but the unions are marriages, one person married to two spouses at once

explanation.surface: A worker who has joined several trade unions.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who weds a second partner while still married is in two marriages at once.

clue.text: A factory worker keeping time nearby

indicators.note: keeping means holding within, so the time letter goes inside

parts.note: a hand is a manual worker, as in factory hand

explanation.surface: A mill employee holding on to the clock close by.
explanation.walkthrough: 'keeping' puts T inside A HAND, after the A.
explanation.definitionFit: Something close at hand is within reach, near.

clue.text: Surveyor's instrument — he tooled it at work

indicators.note: at work means busy being worked on, so these letters are reshaped

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A craftsman made a measuring device by hand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at work' rearranges HE TOOLED IT.
explanation.definitionFit: A theodolite is the tripod-mounted telescope surveyors use to measure angles.

clue.text: US writer in capital — Berlin?

parts.note: Washington is the capital of the United States
Irving Berlin was the American songwriter, so his first name stands in

explanation.surface: An American author living in the German capital, perhaps.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Berlin?' looks like the German capital but is songwriter Irving Berlin; the question mark flags the trick. 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The author of Rip Van Winkle and The Legend of Sleepy Hollow was an American author.

clue.text: A Smiths' composition, about their fifth, a very successful song

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the rearranged letters go round the single letter
a composition is something put together, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, the possessive s being a letter of the band name
their refers to the Smiths, and the fifth letter of Smiths is H

explanation.surface: A song by the Smiths, about their fifth album, becomes a chart-topper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'composition' rearranges A SMITHS, and 'about' puts H, the fifth letter of Smiths, inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A chart-topping single is a popular hit, a song that sells hugely.

clue.text: Black reptile reportedly seen in severe snowstorm

parts.note: B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils

indicators.note: reportedly means as heard, so the reptile word is replaced by one that sounds the same

parts.note: a lizard is a reptile

explanation.surface: A dark-coloured lizard was spotted in a heavy blizzard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reportedly' gives LIZZARD, sounding like LIZARD; 'seen in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A blizzard is a storm of heavy, wind-driven snow.

clue.text: A bet getting one in an excited state

parts.note: a flutter is British slang for a small bet or wager

explanation.surface: A gambler puts money on and gets worked up.
explanation.walkthrough: A FLUTTER is a small bet in British English; 'getting one' links the wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To be fluttering with nerves is to be agitated and excited.

clue.text: M's agent getting villain

parts.note: M is the abbreviation for male, so the letter stands for the full word
a factor is an agent, someone who buys and sells for another

explanation.surface: James Bond's boss M gets a spy who turns out to be a crook.
explanation.walkthrough: 'M's agent' looks like James Bond, but M stands for male here.
explanation.definitionFit: A malefactor is a wrongdoer or criminal, a villain.

clue.text: Commercial outlet in period before Christmas

parts.note: a commercial is an advertisement, an ad
a vent is an outlet for air or steam

explanation.surface: An advert in a shop during the run-up to Christmas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outlet' suggests a shop, but it is an opening, a vent. 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Advent is the church season of the four weeks before Christmas.

clue.text: See 14 across
Resident head leaving Monmouthshire abbey

indicators.note: head leaving means the first letter goes

parts.note: Tintern Abbey is a ruined abbey in Monmouthshire, Wales

explanation.surface: The abbot quits a Welsh abbey.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Resident' suggests a monk but is a junior hospital doctor. TINTERN Abbey is a famous ruin in the Welsh county of Monmouthshire; 'head leaving' drops its T.
explanation.definitionFit: A medical intern is a junior doctor in a hospital; a resident is a similar trainee doctor.

clue.text: Assess greatness at a higher level

parts.note: greatness in the sense of bulk is size
up means at a higher level

explanation.surface: Judge how impressive something is from above.
explanation.definitionFit: To size up a situation is to weigh it up and judge it, so to evaluate it.

clue.text: Come close to touch with ball at end of run

parts.note: two countries that touch share a border, so to touch is to border
O looks like a ball

indicators.note: end of picks the final letter of the word after it

explanation.surface: A cricketer brushes the ball towards the boundary at the end of an innings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'end of' takes N from 'run'; 'with' and 'at' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that borders on madness approaches it, so it nearly reaches it.

clue.text: Home in centre, centre of Baghdad

parts.note: the heart of something is its centre

indicators.note: centre of picks the middle letter of the word after it

explanation.surface: A house in the middle of the Iraqi capital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'centre of' takes H, the fourth of Baghdad's seven letters; 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The fireside stands for the household, so hearth and home are paired.

clue.text: Neighbourhood, note, giving one a second job

parts.note: a side of town is a district or neighbourhood
to drop someone a line is to send a short note

explanation.surface: A note from a local area offers someone extra work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'giving one a' links the wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A sideline is an occupation carried on in addition to one's main work.

clue.text: Members of a house in Stroud moved

indicators.note: moved means shifted about, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Some residents in the Gloucestershire town of Stroud relocated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'house' means a royal dynasty, not a home; Stroud is a town in Gloucestershire. 'moved' rearranges STROUD; 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The Tudor monarchs, Henry VII to Elizabeth I, made up an English royal dynasty.

clue.text: Enclosure with note concerning the US government building

parts.note: a pen is an enclosure for animals
a tag is a label carrying a brief note
on means about, concerning

explanation.surface: A letter with a covering note about the American administration's offices.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Enclosure' suggests something put in an envelope but is a pen for livestock. 'with' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The five-sided headquarters of the US Defense Department in Virginia.
